Sorry for being a little late on this one, but Crunchyroll was airing the Eve no Jikan movie this weekend. Having just watched it and remembering how great this anime is, I thought I'd write up a quick recommendation.

Eve no Jikan is an Asimov-inspired, introspective anime that explores issues of discrimination and prejudice (much like Yoshiura Yasuhiro other works). The movie takes place in a sci-fi setting in which androids are widespread as housekeepers and various other servant-esque professions. Androids can be told apart by the rings above their heads that identify them as such. One day, Masaki Masakuza and Sakisaka Rikuo stumble upon a cafe, called Time of EVE, in which the one rule is that you cannot discriminate between humans and androids. In this cafe, the rings above androids' heads are turned off, making them indistinguishable from humans. Masakuza and Rikuo begin frequenting this cafe, interacting with the regulars and learning how small the gap is between human and android.

Eve no Jikan boasts intriguingly lifelike cinematography, masterful control over dialogue, and delicate portrayal of human expression to articulate a journey through the emotions, motivations, and intentions of androids and humans, more alike than different. If you have time tonight, go watch the movie, which I believe is only on Crunchyroll until tomorrow (for free users, as well, I believe). Otherwise, the OVA should still be on CR for premium users. Once again, sorry for such short notice. I wish I'd thought to put this out there sooner.
I really loved this movie; I appreciate when science fiction asks questions about the ethical implications of things, you know?

It's been a long time since I watched the OVA, so I can't properly evaluate it, but I suspect it gets more praise than it deserves. It's another Asimov rehash, and the ethical questions it raises are IMO on the silly side. It doesn't give any interesting insights on the matter either. It did look great though, and it's well directed enough that it's enjoyable to watch.

Personally, I think Yoshiura's best work yet is Patema Inverted.
